proposals: The Department for Transport should publish advisory headroom guidance for off-highway structures such as forecourt canopies and loading bays, stating plainly that it is not a legal minimum, so designers stop borrowing DMRB CD 127’s trunk-road 5.03m figure by convention and quoting an unsourced 5.4m “modern standard”.

The Department for Transport should collect and publish annual counts and average repair costs of over-height vehicle strikes on non-rail structures, including retail canopies, alongside Network Rail’s bridge-strike figures, so the £10,000–£50,000 per-strike claim in canopy guidance can be checked against data rather than repeated.

The Department for Transport should add a note to Chapter 4 of the Traffic Signs Manual setting out which low-structure signage rules apply to structures on private land approached from the public highway, and how they relate to the 1996 Safety Signs Regulations, so the dual-unit chevron requirement is cited from the right regulation.
